title: The Presbyter's Defense
english: ...To be honored with the call of the episcopate. But perhaps my words may seem harsh and unfriendly to your piety; yet they are not so in truth, for we think to have pity on the presbyter, leaving him only the call, but it would have been much better to consider also the other aspect, for he claims to be able to stand with his own opinion, but not to have had the opportunity for a defense, nor was a canonical hearing added to him. If such a thing had occurred, the composition of the memoranda would have either refuted him, having been found guilty of the charges and having nothing left to say as one who had been wronged, or, having declared him free again, would have given him back the privilege of presiding over the church, which had also been under his care. Since none of this happened, he cries out against the situation, saying that he has suffered unbearable injustice.
translator_notes: The text begins mid-sentence; rendered with a leading ellipsis.
baehrens: PG 77; CPG 5378? Epistula canonica ad Domnum ep rem early

title: The Bishop's Appeal
english: The presbyter was shamelessly exposed, and it was claimed that all belonging to him had been stolen.
Your holiness should consider that this appears to be in accordance with divine canons and what is fitting for the church and those appointed to holy ministry.
Moreover, having considered the letters from us that have entreated you, you should shed a tear for the presbyter at the 279th.

If she chooses to be judged against those bringing charges against her, let her be judged according to the customary practice of your godliness, manifestly with the godly bishops under her hand, unless she refuses some as suspects.

For we believe that none of the godly bishops thinks ill of a brother, in order that this may not become a pretext, the impending judgment upon him being dissolved, so that not in money or possessions.
translator_notes: The Greek text is a fragment, ending mid-sentence at the phrase 'ἐν' (in).

The phrase 'στη 279 σάτω τοῦ πρεσβύту τὸ δάκρυον' is translated literally as 'shed the tear of the presbyter at the 279th', acknowledging the numerical reference likely refers to a page or folio number.
The phrase 'παρ' ἡμῶν δυσωπηθεῖσα γράμματα' is translated as 'the letters from us that have entreated you', treating 'letters' as the object of the beseeching.
The phrase 'ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ παραιτοîτό τινας ὡς ὑπόπτους' is translated as 'unless she refuses some as suspects', interpreting ὑπόπτους in the sense of being under suspicion.
The translation preserves the original agency and modality, with 'under her hand' indicating the bishops are under her authority.
